data.name: DocsLead
data.value: Partnerly is for creating AI agents, giving them tasks, and letting them automate the work.

data.name: DocsStartBody
data.value: You land on Statistics. The sidebar opens the tools you can use — including Plans for your agents — according to your permissions.

data.name: DocsAgentsBody
data.value: Agents live in the sidebar. Create one, open the process editor, put a trigger then actions, save and publish. Pause from the list if you do not want it to run. Plan limits are in Plans at the bottom of the menu. How to fill each block is below.

data.name: DocsUsersBody
data.value: Administrators manage users, roles, and groups. What you can see follows the permissions on your role.

data.name: DocsSettingsBody

data.name: DocsAutomationHowBody
data.value: Open Agents in the sidebar, then +. Name the agent and open the process editor. Put one trigger on the canvas, then actions in order. Click a block — the right panel is where you fill its fields. The same help is under those fields, and the full guide is this page. Save often. Publish so it can run. Pause from the Agents list to stop it without deleting. Run / Test starts a Manual start. Connections shows inbound webhook URLs after publish and saved HTTP bases.

data.name: DocsVariablesBody
data.value: Write placeholders with double curly braces. {{trigger.email}} — a field from the start event. {{vars.order_id}} — a value from Set variable. {{steps.BlockName.result.email}} — output of a previous step. Name the block with letters, digits and underscore. Find record stores the row one level deeper: {{steps.FindUser.result.result.email}}. Passwords, tokens and API secrets cannot be read this way.

data.name: DocsRecordsBody
data.value: User — find and update. Fields: id, email, firstName, lastName, lastActivity, isBlocked, emailConfirmed, roleId, myReferralCode, referrerId, isOnlayn. Support ticket — find, create, update, delete. Fields: id, ticketId, subject, message, status, userId, assignedTo, note. Notification — find and create. Fields: id, type, message, userId, link. User group — find. Fields: id, name. Email template — find. Fields: id, name, subject.

data.name: DocsTriggerManual
data.value: No extra fields. Starts when you click Run or Test. Use this while you are building.

data.name: DocsTriggerSchedule
data.value: How often — Once, at a date (then Run at), Every hour / day / week / month (then Time of day), or Cron expression (example 0 9 * * * for 09:00 every day). After Publish, Partnerly wakes the agent at that time. Time zone is on the agent Settings overlay. Keep the agent active.

data.name: DocsTriggerInterval
data.value: Repeat every (minutes) — minimum 1. The next run is counted from the previous one. Works after Publish while the agent is active.

data.name: DocsTriggerEntityCreated
data.value: Record type — User, Support ticket, Notification, User group, or Email template. Wait before starting — optional amount and unit. Fires when that record is created. Fields of the new row are in {{trigger.…}}.

data.name: DocsTriggerEntityUpdated
data.value: Same Record type and optional Wait before starting as created. Fires when that record is saved. Changed fields are in {{trigger.…}}.

data.name: DocsTriggerEntityDeleted
data.value: Same Record type and optional Wait before starting. Fires when that record is deleted.

data.name: DocsTriggerEvent
data.value: Event name must be exactly one of: UserRegistered — {{trigger.id}}, {{trigger.email}}, {{trigger.firstName}}, {{trigger.lastName}}. UserLoggedIn — same fields; a user signed in. UserLoginFailed — same fields plus {{trigger.attempts}}, {{trigger.lockedOut}}; a wrong password was entered. UserLockedOut — same fields plus {{trigger.lockedUntil}}; the account was locked after too many wrong passwords. UserEmailConfirmed — same fields; the user confirmed the email address. PasswordResetRequested — same fields; a “forgot password” link was sent. PasswordChanged — same fields; the password was changed. UserDeleted — same fields; the user was deleted. SupportTicketCreated — {{trigger.id}}, {{trigger.ticketId}}, {{trigger.subject}}, {{trigger.status}}, {{trigger.type}}. SupportTicketStatusChanged — {{trigger.id}}, {{trigger.ticketId}}, {{trigger.status}}. SupportTicketAssigned — {{trigger.id}}, {{trigger.ticketId}}, {{trigger.subject}}, {{trigger.status}}, {{trigger.assignedTo}}, {{trigger.previousAssignedTo}}. SupportTicketDeleted — {{trigger.id}}, {{trigger.ticketId}}, {{trigger.subject}}, {{trigger.status}}. Wait before starting is optional.

data.name: DocsTriggerWebhook
data.value: After Publish, copy the URL and HMAC secret from Connections. The caller sends POST with header X-Partnerly-Signature. Wait before starting is optional. The body fields are in {{trigger.…}}.

data.name: DocsTriggerDelay
data.value: Wait for — number, at least 1. Unit — seconds, minutes, hours, or days. The workflow starts only after this wait. Use this as the first block when the start itself should be delayed — not the Delay action in the middle of the flow.

data.name: DocsActionsTitle
data.value: Actions — how to configure each step

data.name: DocsActionDelay
data.value: Wait for — number, at least 1. Unit — seconds, minutes, hours, or days. The run pauses, then continues by itself. This is a step in the middle of the flow.

data.name: DocsActionSetVariable
data.value: Variable name — letters, digits, underscore. Value — any text, placeholders allowed. Later steps read it as {{vars.that_name}}.

data.name: DocsActionSendEmail
data.value: Send to — required email. Placeholders such as {{trigger.email}} are allowed. Email template — optional code from Email templates. If set, Subject and Message below are ignored. Subject / Message — used when the template is empty. Default subject is Partnerly.

data.name: DocsActionSendNotification
data.value: Notification text — the in-app message. User id (optional) — a user GUID. Empty sends to the agent owner. Notification type — a label (default System). Link (optional) — URL opened from the notification.

data.name: DocsActionHttpRequest
data.value: HTTP method — GET, POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE. URL — a public http/https address, or a path if Saved connection id is filled (copy the id from Connections). Request body — only for POST, PUT, PATCH. GET and DELETE ignore it. Private or local addresses are blocked.

data.name: DocsActionWebhook
data.value: Webhook URL — public http/https. Partnerly sends POST. JSON body — request body, placeholders allowed. Signing secret (optional) — if set, the request includes header X-Partnerly-Signature (HMAC-SHA256). Same public-URL rule as HTTP request.

data.name: DocsActionExecuteWorkflow
data.value: Child automation id — GUID of another agent you own that is published. This step starts it and does not wait for it to finish.

data.name: DocsActionBranch
data.value: Left value, Compare, Right value. Operators: equals, not equals, contains, greater than, less than, is empty, is not empty, changed. Placeholders allowed in Left and Right. Connect two links from the block: first output is True, second is False.

data.name: DocsActionWaitUntil
data.value: Same condition fields as Branch, plus Give up after (optional deadline). The run waits until the condition is true or the deadline passes. Empty deadline keeps checking.

data.name: DocsActionSwitch
data.value: Value to match — placeholders allowed. Empty value uses the first output (default). Connect the second output for the other case.

data.name: DocsActionCreateRecord
data.value: Record type, then Fields (one per line, for example subject=Hello). Create works only for Support ticket (subject, message, status, userId, assignedTo, note) and Notification (type, message, userId, link). User, User group and Email template cannot be created here.

data.name: DocsActionUpdateRecord
data.value: Record type. Which record — one key per line, for example id={{trigger.id}}. Fields — values to change. Update works for User (firstName, lastName, isBlocked) and Support ticket (subject, status, assignedTo, note).

data.name: DocsActionFindRecord
data.value: Record type and Filters (one per line, for example email={{trigger.email}} or id={{trigger.id}}). Works for User, Support ticket, Notification, User group and Email template. Name the block with letters and digits. The found row is {{steps.BlockName.result.result.email}}.

data.name: DocsActionDeleteRecord
data.value: Record type and Which record (one key per line, for example id={{trigger.id}}). Delete is allowed for Support ticket.

data.name: DocsIntegrationComputer
data.value: Lets agents act on your own Windows PC through the small Partnerly Agent program (an icon in the tray). Setup: open Integrations, press Add in the Computer card and press Create. Download the program with your settings from the next window (the token is shown once), unzip it, start Partnerly.Agent.exe and press Yes to install it for your Windows account. It needs Windows 10 or newer and nothing else. Everything is decided on the PC, in the settings file (tray menu, Open settings file): allowedFolders - folders cards may read, write, copy, zip and open; allowedPrograms - programs cards may run or close; scriptFolders - folders with .ps1 / .bat / .cmd scripts; watchFolders and watchPrograms - what is reported to the triggers; confirmOps - commands that first ask for a click on the PC, for example run_program, lock or sleep. Whatever is not listed is refused. Actions: notification, message window, speak text, open link / file / folder, copy and read clipboard, PC information, screenshot, is a program running, read and write text file, list folder, copy, move, zip, save an attachment to the PC, get a file from the PC (it becomes an attachment, so a Telegram or Drive card can send it), run program, run script, close program, lock, sleep. Triggers: new file on PC, PC went online or offline, program started on PC. Left out on purpose: free commands, keystrokes and mouse, the registry, deleting files. If the PC is off, the card fails with a clear message, and the agent can use the error path.

data.name: BuilderIntPcFileCreatedIntro

data.name: BuilderIntPcFileChangedIntro

data.name: BuilderIntPcFileDeletedIntro

data.name: ComputerWait
data.value: Waiting for the program to connect...

data.name: ComputerConnectedOk
data.value: Connected! "{0}" is online. You can close this window.

data.name: ComputerWaitLong
data.value: Still nothing. Check that the program is running (icon near the clock) and open "Why is it offline?" under the computer in the list.

data.name: ComputerTrouble1
data.value: The program is not running: look for its icon near the clock (click the small arrow if it is hidden). If it is not there, start Partnerly.Agent.exe again.

data.name: ComputerTrouble2
data.value: It is turned off: right-click the icon and tick "Let Partnerly use this computer". The card then says "Paused on the PC".

data.name: ComputerTrouble3
data.value: The PC is asleep, switched off, or has no internet.

data.name: ComputerTrouble4
data.value: The token was renewed (key button) or this computer was deleted here and added again: download the program with the new settings and start it, or use "Connection..." in the tray menu.

data.name: ComputerTrouble5
data.value: The program was removed from the PC (the card says "Program removed"): download it and install it again.

data.name: ComputerTrouble6
data.value: Still stuck? Right-click the icon and choose "Check connection": it says in plain words what is wrong.

data.name: ComputerTokenStep1
data.value: Press the button below to download the program with your settings (a zip file).

data.name: ComputerTokenStep2
data.value: Open the Downloads folder, right-click the zip and choose "Extract All". Do not start the program from inside the zip.

data.name: ComputerTokenStep3
data.value: Open the new folder, start Partnerly.Agent.exe and press Yes. It installs for your Windows account.

data.name: ComputerTokenStep4
data.value: Wait here: this window turns green when the computer is connected.

data.name: DocsIntegrationComputerMore
data.value: The program lives in the tray (near the clock): a green dot means connected. Right-click it to turn Partnerly's access on or off, change folders, programs and watching in Settings, check the connection, or remove the program (also possible in Windows Settings > Apps). Triggers: new, changed or deleted file, program started or closed, screen locked or unlocked, PC woke up, USB drive plugged, charger or battery, nobody at the PC, disk space low, clipboard text. Actions: files (read, write, copy, move, zip, unzip, Recycle Bin, download), programs and scripts, notifications and windows, volume and media buttons, screenshot, lock, sleep, shut down. If the computer shows offline, open "Why is it offline?" under it in the list.

data.name: ComputerErrOffline
data.value: The computer is offline. Start Partnerly Agent on it and try again.

data.name: ComputerErrTimeout
data.value: The computer did not answer in time.

data.name: ComputerErrWentOffline
data.value: The computer went offline while the command was running.
